subject: MedScale security discovery: KMS & encryption follow-up
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Emma Durand <emma.durand@medscale.com>
Cc: Raj Patel <raj.patel@medscale.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: MedScale security discovery: KMS & encryption follow-up

Hi Emma — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we have alignment.

Key points we covered: 
- SOC 2 status: you mentioned MedScale completed Type I and are targeting Type II by Q3. Please confirm the auditor and approximate evidence windows you expect us to need.
- GDPR / HIPAA: primary requirement is role-based access auditing and data residency for EU patients; you flagged some HIPAA controls for logging and retention.
- Encryption: you asked about at-rest and in-transit protections, support for customer-managed keys (BYOK), and HSM-backed key custody.

Specific asks we have to answer for your security team: 
1) Provide a short architecture diagram showing where keys are stored and how traffic flows (we can share a sanitized public link).
2) Confirm whether Redwood can support customer-managed CMKs (BYOK) with HSM-backed wrapping and give a short matrix of feature tradeoffs (rotation, exportability, backup).
3) Provide SOC 2 artifacts/summary (what we can share publicly) and a timeline for anything under NDA.
4) Complete your vendor security questionnaire — if you can send it, we’ll assign owners and return answers within 3 business days for the first pass.

Next steps I propose: 
- Emma: send over the vendor questionnaire and any preferred evidence format (zip, Drive folder).
- Marcusside: we’ll prepare a one-page KMS comparison (Redwood-managed vs BYOK) and a sanitized architecture diagram.
- Schedule a follow-up (30 min) with your security lead to walk the questionnaire answers.

I’ve CC’d Raj since he’ll be involved in procurement discussions for Dedicated/Private options. Monica and Aditya are on the thread internally to own the artifacts.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood-kms-implementation-notes.pdf (pdf, 320KB)]

From: Emma Durand <emma.durand@medscale.com>

Cc: MedScale Security <security@medscale.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@medscale.com>
Date: Tue, 02 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: MedScale security discovery: KMS & encryption follow-up

Thanks Marcus — great summary. A few clarifications and I attached our vendor security questionnaire to this reply.

Clarifications: 
- SOC 2: we used BrightAudit for the Type I and are in the process of scoping Type II with the same firm. Our security team typically requests a letter of attestation plus the controls matrix. If you can indicate which artifacts are public vs. require an NDA that’ll speed things up.
- BYOK: we require HSM-backed key wrapping for production patient data; rotation policies must be controllable by our security admin.
- Logging & retention: our HIPAA reviewers want 12 months of immutable access logs and 6 years of retention for certain audit artifacts.

Attached: MedScale_Vendor_Security_Questionnaire_2027.docx
We’d like answers to the questionnaire in the next 3 business days if possible. Also can you share your architecture diagram as a Drive link so our infra team can quickly review?

Available for a follow-up Thurs 3/4 between 10–11am ET or Fri 3/5 2–4pm ET.

— Emma
Emma Durand
Head of IT Security
MedScale

Owners: 
- Monica: SOC 2 artifacts, controls matrix, and redaction guidance (ETA: 48 hours)
- Aditya: KMS feature matrix + HSM details, key rotation docs, and public architecture diagram link (ETA: 48 hours)

If you expect any blockers (e.g., we need legal to approve redactions), flag now so I can set expectations with Emma. I’ll draft the cover email to include the DocuSign/HubSpot links and send when the artifacts are ready.

— Marcus

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: MedScale security discovery: KMS & encryption follow-up

Hi Emma — following up with the artifacts we discussed. Links and attachments below.

Provided items (first pass): 
- redwood-kms-implementation-notes.pdf — short matrix comparing Redwood-managed keys vs BYOK with HSM wrap, rotation cadence, and export constraints. (attached)
- Architecture diagram (sanitized): https://drive.example.com/file/d/1a2b3c-redwood-arch — public view. If you need the private version we’ll request NDA and provide a private folder.
- SOC 2 summary: we can share our public SOC 2 letter (Type II in progress). Monica included a controls snapshot in the attached PDF; anything that needs an NDA is flagged.

A couple of notes on the KMS options: 
- BYOK with HSM wrapping: supported. Keys are imported into an HSM-backed module and wrapped with a customer CMK. Rotation is customer-controlled; we recommend a 90-day rotation cadence for keys used to encrypt PHI.
- Redwood-managed keys: offers simpler ops (no customer key import needed) and automated rotation, but key export is not allowed. We can provide attestations around key separation and access controls.

Next actions: 
- We’ll return the completed questionnaire answers as a marked-up doc by EOD Fri 3/5.
- Please confirm which artifacts require NDA so Monica can route to Legal.
- Proposed follow-up call: Thurs 3/4 10:30am ET — does 10:30–11:00am ET work for you and your security lead?

Thanks — looking forward to closing the discovery.

— Marcus
